description: Combines deep level ratio (L3-5 vs L1-5) with L1 book imbalance. Original hypothesis (agreement confirms MM positioning) FAILED. Discovered CONTRARIAN variant: when deep liquidity and L1 imbalance agree bullish, bet Down (and vice versa). Deep liquidity layering appears to be deceptive — MMs layer visible depth opposite to intended direction. Spread>=75pct filter HURTS the contrarian signal (edge exists in tighter-spread markets).
hypothesis: Original hypothesis (agreement = confirmation) FAILED — deep_ratio_diff is negatively correlated with outcomes (r=-0.08). Contrarian variant at threshold 0.10 shows 58.65% WR on 104 trades (z=1.76, p=0.039 unadjusted). However, after Bonferroni correction for ~14 parameter combinations tested, p=0.55 — NOT statistically significant. The sensitivity analysis is non-monotonic (threshold 0.12 drops to 53.7% WR), suggesting the 0.10 sweet spot may be overfitting. The buy_down side (62.3% WR) carries most of the edge; buy_up (54.9% WR) is weak.
next_steps: Edge is suggestive but not statistically robust after multiple testing correction. Critical next step: validate on full 7187-market dataset (out-of-sample test). If contrarian edge persists at WR>55% with n>300, it becomes credible. Also investigate: (1) why buy_down is stronger than buy_up (base rate asymmetry or genuine signal?), (2) rate-of-change of deep ratio rather than level, (3) temporal stability across different market regimes.
